title: Google finally releases Gemini 4 Argon
key_facts: Google began rolling out Gemini 4 Argon on 13 Oct 2026 to its higher-tier Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and in AI mode in Search, and to Ultra subscribers on its agentic development platform Antigravity.
It is not clear when, or if, Argon will reach Plus subscribers or free users.
Google says Argon outperforms GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 on benchmarks covering coding, cybersecurity, science, finance and law (Google's own claim).

Introductory price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth of the cost of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Fable 5 models; the price doubles at the end of November when the introductory period ends.
The Verge cautions that a lower per-token price does not necessarily mean lower real costs, because models can use different numbers of tokens for the same task.
The public rollout follows a limited release to a select set of 'trusted cyber defenders' to test for potential risks.

Google says it already uses Argon internally to find and patch security vulnerabilities, to halve the computing power for YouTube's comments section and to debug the drone physics simulator of Alphabet's drone delivery company Wing.
Argon is Google's first major frontier release since Gemini 3 in late 2025; it landed a day after Meta announced its Muse Wonder Full model.
quote_evidence: The model is rolling out today to Google’s higher-tier Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI mode in Search, as well to Ultra subscribers on its agentic development platform Antigravity.
It is not clear when — or if — Argon will be available to Plus subscribers or free users.
In line with other recent frontier model releases, the public rollout follows a limited release to a select set of “trusted cyber defenders” to be tested for potential risks.
why_it_matters_hint: Paying Gemini users can now use Google's newest top model, priced well below its main rivals, but the performance claims are Google's own.
